decisive_items: pathogenic variant in the FH gene (FHc.999C > A p.Cys333Ter)
Prominent eosinophilic nucleoli with perinucleolar halo
response.rationale: FH loss with a pathogenic FH germline-type variant in a spindle-cell smooth-muscle tumor establishes HLRCC syndrome; the large pelvic mass is a syndromic leiomyoma rather than an isolated or ovarian tumor, and the breast nodules are not the primary diagnosis.

rejected.why: Essentially the same entity as R4 but less explicitly syndromic and adds no independent evidence beyond the shared FH variant.
Uterine leiomyoma is a component of HLRCC but fails to account for the defining FH loss and FH pathogenic variant.
Atypical leiomyoma morphology is present but is only descriptive; the genetic and IHC findings point to HLRCC syndrome.
Ovarian origin is not convincing given the uterine/anatomical findings and is incompatible with the FH-loss syndromic context.
Only addresses incidental breast fibroadenomas and cannot explain the pelvic mass, histology, or FH mutation.
